clue.text: Indian garments making one very warm in the lower regions

indicators.note: in places the word for very warm inside the name for the underworld

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, the lower regions
very warm means hot

explanation.surface: Loincloths that leave the wearer overheated below the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the Roman underworld and its god, so 'the lower regions' is a proper name here; 'in' is the container signal and 'making one' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the loincloth worn by many Hindu men in India, here in the plural.

clue.text: Hard time for the queen

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A tough spell for the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Hera was queen of the gods, wife of Zeus.

clue.text: That was clever, Paisley's party being revamped

parts.note: touché is said to acknowledge a clever point scored against you
Ian Paisley led the DUP, the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A remark admiring how Ian Paisley's party has been given a makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Something touched up has been improved with small changes, much as something revamped is renovated.

clue.text: Miss Woodhouse sanctified in the family tree

parts.note: a sanctified person is a saint, abbreviated ST
Emma Woodhouse is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel Emma

explanation.surface: Jane Austen's heroine is made a saint in her own genealogy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Woodhouse sanctified' becomes St Emma, so ST comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A stemma is a pedigree or genealogical chart, a family tree.

clue.text: Offensive series of articles by fellow without name

parts.note: the articles an, a and the in a row

indicators.note: without means the letter for name is dropped from the word for fellow

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A string of distasteful pieces written by a nameless man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops N from MAN, leaving MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anathema to you is utterly detestable, so deeply offensive.

clue.text: Statute inapt — malefactor should be dealt with

indicators.note: dealt with suggests cards being reshuffled and redistributed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a law is unsuitable and the wrongdoer should be punished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be dealt with' rearranges the fifteen letters of INAPT MALEFACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of parliament is a law passed by the legislature, a statute.

clue.text: Ace Introduction to Prayer for girl's confirmation

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter, here of Prayer

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
Val is a girl's name; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A girl's first prayer leads to her religious confirmation.
explanation.definitionFit: Approval is official sanction or endorsement, a confirmation that something is accepted.

clue.text: PM's passion beginning to repeat itself

parts.note: heat means intense passion
the opening letter of the word for passion comes again at the end

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister's enthusiasm starting to recur.
explanation.walkthrough: The H of HEAT repeats itself after HEAT; the 's of PM's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Heath was the British Conservative Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974.

clue.text: Second country almost adjoins that French country

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the country is missing

parts.note: Zambia is a country in southern Africa
que is French for that

explanation.surface: One nation next to another, which is next to a French one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last A from ZAMBIA, giving ZAMBI; 'adjoins' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozambique is a nation in south-east Africa, bordering Zambia.

clue.text: Contretemps are not shortened when stick is introduced

indicators.note: is introduced means the word for stick is put inside the contraction

parts.note: are not contracted becomes aren't
gum means to stick or glue

explanation.surface: A disagreement over contracted words and sticking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' signals the contraction of 'are not' with its apostrophe, not a cut; 'is introduced' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A contretemps is a minor dispute or row, an argument.

clue.text: Something edible in form of circle circumscribing a square

indicators.note: circumscribing means drawn around, so the food goes round the letter A

parts.words: Something edible in form of circle
parts.note: a pizza is a round food

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle: a round food item drawn around a square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circumscribing' puts PIZZA around A; the geometric surface makes 'square' look like a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A piazza is an open public square, especially in an Italian town.

clue.text: In terrible form in a place where one should feel comfortable

definitions.text: a place where one should feel comfortable

parts.note: at home means in

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters of the word form are scrambled

parts.note: home again means in, as in staying at home

explanation.surface: Feeling out of sorts in a spot where one ought to be at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' appears twice, each time standing for the same word meaning at one's residence; 'terrible' is the anagram signal on 'form'.
explanation.definitionFit: A home from home is somewhere one feels as relaxed as in one's own house.

clue.text: Male speaker, I have hesitation and freeze

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A man giving a speech hesitates and seizes up.
explanation.definitionFit: A moratorium is a temporary suspension or halt, as in a freeze on spending.

clue.text: What are you trying to do? Don't get angry! Promise!

definitions.text: What are you trying to do? Don't get angry! Promise!

parts.words: What are you trying to do? Don't get angry! Promise!
parts.note: solvers trying to find an entry are trying to get the right term; a calming plea for a vow to keep calm is giving one's solemn pledge

explanation.surface: Someone flustered, pleading for calm and a pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: The first question describes the solver hunting for the entry; 'Promise!' is the plain sense, as in giving one's pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A word is a promise, as in giving one's word, and the solver is always seeking a term.

clue.text: He would present Prime Minister T. Blair as ace — all spinning?

definitions.text: He would present Prime Minister T. Blair as ace — all spinning?

indicators.note: spinning means turning round, so the letters are rearranged, with a nod to political spin

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's spin doctor would make the PM look a star by spinning everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' rearranges PM, T, BLAIR, AS, ACE and ALL; the whole clue also describes Blair's press secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Alastair Campbell was Tony Blair's director of communications, notorious as his spin doctor.

clue.text: What is human but loveless — one politician establishing dominion

indicators.note: loveless means the letter O, love being zero in tennis, is taken out of the proverb's words

parts.note: to err is human, as the proverb says
I is the Roman numeral one
a Tory is a Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A proverb about human failings applied to a politician seizing power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' removes O from TO ERR, leaving TERR.
explanation.definitionFit: A territory is land under a ruler's control, a dominion.

clue.text: Musical sequences must have musical quality in principle

parts.note: keys are the tonal systems or scales music is written in
tone is the quality of a musical sound

explanation.surface: A music lesson on scales and timbre.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystone is the central principle on which everything else depends.

clue.text: See 14
Herb is said to be in this sauce mixture

indicators.note: is said signals a word that sounds like the herb

parts.note: rue is a bitter herb

explanation.surface: A cooking note that a certain herb belongs in this sauce base.
explanation.definitionFit: A roux is a cooked mixture of fat and flour used to thicken sauces.

clue.text: Elf shows malice crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means the word for malice spans the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: spite is malice

explanation.surface: A spiteful elf crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is a fairy or elf.

clue.text: Supports rock duo with pianist keeping pianissimo

indicators.note: keeping means holding the musical abbreviation inside the scrambled letters
to rock is to shake, so the letters of duo and pianist are shaken up

parts.note: pp is the musical marking for pianissimo, very softly

explanation.surface: A rock band of two members plus a pianist who plays very quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock duo' poses as a band, but 'rock' is the anagram signal on 'duo' and 'pianist'; 'keeping' is the container signal for the musical marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Points d'appui are bases or props, supports for an operation, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Girl is a "bird", as some might say

indicators.note: as some might say signals a pronunciation in accents that drop the final r

parts.note: a bird that builds a nest is a nester

explanation.surface: Someone's girlfriend called a bird in slang.
explanation.walkthrough: In accents that drop a final R, NESTER sounds like NESTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesta is a female given name, mostly Welsh.

clue.text: Plant settler in Kent

definitions.meaning: a fibre plant used for sacking
the ... were a Germanic people who settled in Kent in the fifth century

explanation.surface: A plant grown by an incomer to Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Jute is a fibre plant; a Jute was one of the people who settled Kent.

clue.text: Time lost from orders — firm in ruin

indicators.note: lost from means the time letter is dropped from the word for orders

parts.note: fiats are decrees or orders
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A firm's collapse after delayed orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost from' removes T from FIATS, leaving FIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating failure, a complete ruin of plans.

clue.text: Holy record found in European community — English message of a religious nature?

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the abbreviation for the European grouping

parts.note: EU is the European Union, a community of states
pi is short for pious, holy
a log is a record

explanation.surface: A sacred document turns up in Europe and carries an English religious message.
explanation.walkthrough: The Epilogue was a short religious talk that closed British TV broadcasting each night, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue was a closing religious talk at the end of a broadcasting day.

clue.text: Returning three years ago, getting about here, there and everywhere

indicators.note: returning means the Roman date is read backwards

parts.note: this 2004 puzzle makes three years ago 2001, MMI in Roman numerals
anent means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Coming back after three years and travelling all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns MMI into IMM; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immanent is present throughout, pervading all things everywhere.

clue.text: Palace in place that has its own clue

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
a see is a cathedral city's diocese, and 'See' is literally printed as a clue for linked entries

explanation.surface: A palace located somewhere that gets its own crossword hint.
explanation.walkthrough: Linked entries carry the clue 'See 14' and the like, so 'See' has its own clue; ELY is a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Élysée Palace in Paris is the official residence of the French president.
